title: Infrastructure as Code

searches.query: Infrastructure as Code production interview Terraform state locking drift partial apply
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: Terraform: State
sources.supportRationale: IaC state maps managed configuration to real infrastructure and can contain sensitive information.

sources.title: Terraform: State locking
sources.supportRationale: Backend-dependent state locking coordinates writers and force-unlock needs ownership evidence.

sources.title: Terraform: Plan command
sources.supportRationale: A plan predicts actions against selected inputs; saved versus speculative plans have different application paths.

sources.title: Terraform: Apply command
sources.supportRationale: Apply executes provider operations and partial failure does not imply global transactional rollback.

sources.title: Terraform: Manage resource drift
sources.supportRationale: Out-of-band changes require explicit refresh/reconciliation decisions.

sources.title: Terraform: Import existing resources
sources.supportRationale: Import maps existing provider objects to configuration/state; it is not a permission to recreate them.

sources.title: Terraform: Provider requirements
sources.supportRationale: Selected provider identity and version requirements constrain plan/apply behavior.

scenarios.theme: A lock delays a second operator during an incident. Should it be disabled?
scenarios.assumptions: Two applies target the same state. One terminal appears idle but a cloud API operation may still run. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Infrastructure as Code to concurrent state.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A lock delays a second operator during an incident. Should it be disabled?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Identify the current operation and owner, coordinate its completion/termination and inspect real effects before any supported unlock/recovery

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Waiting has incident cost, but bypassing an active lock can corrupt assumptions or state

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Force-unlock requires ownership evidence; losing a terminal is not proof the provider action stopped.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to locking, apply; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The CLI hides a password, but the state file contains it. What controls are needed?
scenarios.assumptions: A teammate proposes committing state because values marked sensitive are masked in normal output. What response fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Infrastructure as Code to state secret.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The CLI hides a password, but the state file contains it. What controls are needed?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Treat state and saved plans as sensitive, use access-controlled storage with appropriate encryption/version recovery and avoid committing exports

scenarios.theme: Two independent IaC states keep changing the same firewall rule. Which lock fixes it?
scenarios.assumptions: Each state locks correctly, but one team’s apply reverts the other team’s change. What ownership model fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Infrastructure as Code to two owners.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Two independent IaC states keep changing the same firewall rule. Which lock fixes it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Assign a single management owner or split truly independent resource boundaries, represent dependencies explicitly and reconcile desired policy in one plac

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Per-state locks do not coordinate unrelated owners of one remote object

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Larger shared state simplifies some coordination but broadens blast radius and access; choose boundaries based on actual lifecycle ownership.
